old_caption: The video captures a serene rural scene featuring a rustic wooden shed situated on a grassy lawn. The shed, weathered and aged, has a metal roof and a stone foundation, suggesting it might be used for storage or as a workshop. In front of the shed, a pile of branches and twigs is burning brightly, with flames licking up and smoke rising into the air. To the right of the shed, a dark-colored SUV is parked, partially obscured by the tree. A large tree stands prominently behind the vehicle, its leaves rustling gently in the breeze. Nearby, a blue barrel and a concrete mixer are visible, hinting at ongoing or recent construction or maintenance work. The sky above is partly cloudy, allowing patches of sunlight to filter through, casting dappled shadows across the scene. The overall atmosphere is calm and peaceful, with no visible movement or activity other than the steady burn of the fire.

caption: The video captures an outdoor yard on a partly cloudy day, where a fire is already burning at the base of a brush pile in the center foreground. A weathered wooden barn stands to the left, and a large leafy tree fills the center and right, its lower branches hovering above the flames. Behind the pile sits a pale shipping container, with blue barrels and a blue tarp to its left, a stack of lumber to its right, a dark SUV parked under the tree, and a round metal tank at the far right. The orange flames flicker and reshape continuously, their height varying as they rise and fall above the brush. A translucent plume of smoke drifts upward and slightly right from the fire, its density and position shifting as the burn continues. The brush pile, barn, tree, vehicle, container, and tank remain in place, and the camera viewpoint remains essentially fixed. The fire persists as an ongoing burn, and the flames and smoke carry the main motion across the otherwise still scene.

endpoints are normal, not physical errors. Do not add unseen causes, onset, stopping or outcomes.
An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

Check identification before physical interpretation: a reflection is not a separate actor;
a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.
Do not claim contact, bending, compression, melting, disintegration or structural recovery unless
the appropriate material/surface itself provides visible evidence. Do not infer a force or earlier
collision just because the visible configuration would be compatible with it.
Compare several frames before asserting translation, rotation, direction, unchanged position or
camera tracking. A single visible texture/seam does not prove spin. Avoid unnecessary absolute
claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.
Remove invented scene details and explanations, but keep clearly visible ongoing motion and
processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.

Retain the WISA English narrative style, detail density and paragraph structure. Aim for the
provided original word count within 85%-115%, using genuinely visible details and process.
Do not add repetition, watermark/logo descriptions or atmospheric filler to reach a word count.

'this mid-segment', 'the excerpt', 'the frame', 'these images', 'observed evidence' in the caption.
This is a direct video description, not an analysis note. No mandatory beginning/end formula.
Complete every sentence. If accuracy requires a substantial length difference, explain it outside
the caption; do not fill missing context by imagination. Optional synonym edits are not needed.
